answer: Each account may submit jobs, but a settlement contract releases payment only after a randomly selected verifier reproduces the result and stakes tokens that are forfeited if its verdict conflicts with later checks. A falcon can spot a hollow cluster of newly minted identities, yet the contract does not trust identity labels: splitting one operator across many agents still requires funding each stake and paying for each verified job. The atlas of accounts can grow, but a Sybil attacker must lock real capital and risk losing it per dishonest claim.
